full_judgment: 6. Mr. Shah Md. Khasruzumman, the learned Advocate appearing with Ms. Reshma Sultana on behalf of the petitioners contends that the judgment of the trial court and that of the appellate court clearly shows that 17½ decimals of land out of total 35 decimals of land of C.S. Khatian no.88 were acquired and admittedly Jamuna Bibi transferred her share to Sun Shine Cable Mills. and rest of the land i.e. the suit land comprising 17½ decimals was acquired by the Government and belongs to RAJUK. Mr. Kharuzzaman contends that after the admitted transfer of 17½ of land Sun Shine Cable Mills. by Jamuna Bibi no land was left in the suit plot other then the suit land measuring17½  decimals only and this land was acquired by the Government and the land of Sun Shine Cable Mills was never acquired by the Government but the appellate court did ,not consider the same. He further contends that certificate of delivery of possession ( Ext. Ka) is enough to prove that the suit land had been acquired by the Government and not the land of Sun Shine Cable Mills and it is not also the case of the plaintiffs. He also invited my attention to the joint inventory of L.A. case no. 8/64-65(Ext. Kha) and also to the testimony of the witnesses specially P.W.5 and contends that the appellate court committed an error of law in not considering the aforesaid material evidence on record resulting in an error in the decision in allowing the appeal. He further contends that since the plaintiffs claimed that the suit plot was never acquired by the Government, the plaintiffs should have made the acquiring body i.e. the Government of Bangladesh a party to the suit but they intentionally avoided to do so.
